newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges Arab League to end Turkish attack.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges Arab League to end Turkish attack.

text.p: Iraq on Thursday urged the Arab League to put an end to a Turkish incursion into north Iraq and warned that it reserved the right to retaliate "against Turkish aggressive acts."

Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammad Saeed al-Sahaf, in a letter to the Arab League carried by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), said Turkish forces push into the north in pursuit of Kurdish guerrillas has caused several causualties among Iraqi Kurds.
"In his letter, the Foreign Minister called on the Arab League to shoulder its responsibility and prevent (Turkish) threats and aggression," INA said.
"Iraq reserves its legitimate rights under international law to retaliate against Turkish aggressive acts and demands compensation for the damage caused by the incursions," Sahaf said.
Several thousand Turkish troops, backed by tanks and heavy artillery, pushed across the border into northern Iraq on Wednesday in a sweep against separatist Kurdish rebel bases.
"Turkish troops' practices such as shelling Iraq villages and illegally entering Iraqi territory are a flagrant violation of Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity," the foreign minister said.

Turkish security sources told Reuters 30 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels and four soldiers were killed in the first two days of the Iraq operation, most in the early hours before dawn on Wednesday.
